sense: to make something by putting parts together

pins.definition: To make something by putting parts together, especially a building or structure.
To make a building, structure, or object by putting parts together.
To make a structure such as a house, road, or bridge by putting parts together.

situation: A carpenter in a bright workshop is assembling a wooden birdhouse on a worktable.
subject: the assembled structure
brief: A half-completed wooden birdhouse sits on a workbench, surrounded by neatly cut individual walls, roof panels, and small pegs waiting to be joined. The maker's hands are placing the final side wall into its slot, showing the process of parts coming together into a solid structure.
prompt: A half-completed wooden birdhouse sits on a workbench, surrounded by neatly cut individual walls, roof panels, and small pegs waiting to be joined. The maker's hands are placing the final side wall into its slot, showing the process of parts coming together into a solid structure. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
